description: Eleven documented observational images and provisional instructional examples; limitations disclosed. Final physical primer and consent-specific photography remain separate.

images.title: Counting with physical beads
images.summary: A photographed abacus illustrates discrete objects and quantities.
images.alt: Red beads in rows on rods in a frame.
images.caption: Provisional counting example: movable beads represent quantities under human conventions. A dedicated one-to-ten arrangement is still preferable for the universal primer.

images.summary: Several herbivorous mammals at a wildlife sanctuary in Uganda.
images.alt: Elephant, antelope and zebra in a vegetated enclosure.
images.caption: Different animals have different typical body dimensions. Perspective and distance prevent this photograph from providing exact size ratios.

images.alt: Rounded grey stones of many sizes on a beach.
images.caption: Provisional natural tonal-contrast example; the image contains intermediate shades and is not a two-state binary calibration target.

images.title: Microscopic light-harvesting structures
images.summary: Published scientific figure combining electron micrographs and interpretive diagrams of bacterial light-harvesting structures.
images.alt: Colored diagrams above grayscale electron microscopy panels with scale bars.
images.caption: The micrographs show observed cellular structures; the colored panels are explanatory models, not photographs. Source: Nature Communications 7, 12454 (2016), doi:10.1038/ncomms12454.
images.credit: J. Nielsen, N. Kulminskaya, M. Bjerring et al.
images.rights: CC BY 4.0; https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/. Credit source article and authors.

images.title: Microbial mats in a hot spring
images.summary: A close view of microbial mats near Grand Prismatic Spring, Yellowstone.
images.alt: Orange-brown textured mats in shallow water.
images.caption: Microbes form communities in geothermal water. This habitat photograph does not identify a specific species or establish that any other archived microscope specimen was collected here; independent cell observations appear elsewhere in the collection.
images.rights: CC BY-SA 3.0, Daniel Mayer; https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/. Archive derivative retains this license.

images.title: Salt-loving microbes and their environments
images.summary: Published multi-panel photographic figure showing hypersaline habitats and a microscopic sample from Lake Tyrrell.
images.alt: Satellite salt ponds, field observations, colored microscopic cells, layered mineral crust and a lab sample.
images.caption: The microscopic panel tentatively identifies square haloarchaeal cells alongside green algae; the other panels show distinct hypersaline environments, not necessarily the exact sampling site. Scale bar 5 micrometers. Source article doi:10.1111/1751-7915.13576.
images.credit: Terry J. McGenity et al.; NASA (A), Great Salt Lake Institute (B,C,G), Mike Dyall-Smith (D), Andreas Thywißen (E)

images.title: Human internal organs in a teaching model
images.summary: A life-size educational model of the human head and torso made by the German Hygiene Museum in Dresden.
images.alt: Painted anatomical model showing skull, lungs, heart, liver and intestines.
images.caption: The model shows the relative positions of major organs. It is not a photograph of living tissue and does not include the whole body; compare the archived skeleton image.

images.title: Three generations of a human family
images.summary: National Cancer Institute photograph of three related adult women.
images.alt: Three women of different adult generations together beneath a shelter.
images.caption: Humans grow and age, and families can span multiple generations. This portrait shows adult life stages, not the entire human lifespan.
images.rights: US National Cancer Institute image marked public domain with no reuse restrictions; credit Bill Branson / NCI. Separate model release is not established; review before flight.

images.alt: Family members gathered around a kitchen counter with vegetables.
images.caption: Humans prepare food using shared work, tools and domestic spaces. One US household scene from 1989 is not representative of all cultures.
